_note: Informal Italian, slang and swear words in Italy (/conoscenze/gergo). Own draft, idioms-mistakes run (2026-11-14), not yet reviewed. reg: umgang (informal) | slang | vulgaer (rude); stufe (vulgaer only): 1 mild, 2 strong, 3 very strong. w, bsp and the hoeflich pairs are Italian; std is the standard word with its English meaning; info is English. variety it-IT on every entry. No slurs and no insults about groups of people (content-plan §5.7). Regional slang (Rome, Naples, Milan) is left out on purpose.

stufen.name: Rude
stufen.satz: Hai due minuti o cosa, cazzo?

gruppen.titel: Short forms: how people really speak
gruppen.intro: In everyday speech, words get shorter. Don't write these forms in a letter or an exam, but you will hear them every day.

eintraege.bsp: Il prof ci ha dato troppi compiti.
eintraege.info: Used by students and everybody about school and university teachers. In a letter write professore.

eintraege.bsp: Vado al lavoro in bici.
eintraege.info: Neutral enough for any speech; in writing both forms are fine.

eintraege.bsp: C'è del latte nel frigo?
eintraege.info: Normal in speech. Same for la tele (televisione) and l'uni (università).

eintraege.bsp: Non è venuto? Vabbè, andiamo senza di lui.
eintraege.info: Often means oh well: it shows you accept something you don't love. It is written vabbè or vabbe', never with a full stop.

eintraege.bsp: 'Sera, signora Rossi! Tutto bene?
eintraege.info: A shortened greeting with neighbours and shopkeepers you know. With officials, say the full word.

eintraege.bsp: Aspetta un po', arrivo subito.
eintraege.info: Always written with an apostrophe: un po', not un pò. It is standard, not slang, but learners often get the spelling wrong.

eintraege.bsp: 'Spetta, non ho ancora finito!
eintraege.info: Only in fast speech between friends. Write aspetta.

eintraege.bsp: Domani ho lezione all'uni alle nove.
eintraege.info: Student speech. Also la prof, la mensa, la bibliot.

gruppen.intro: These words are relaxed, but not rude. With friends and colleagues they are normal. In a formal letter or at an office, use the word on the right.

eintraege.bsp: Che ora è? – Boh, non ho l'orologio.
eintraege.info: A one-syllable shrug, very common. Not for a formal situation, but everybody says it.

eintraege.std: non… affatto; per caso (not at all; by any chance)
eintraege.bsp: Non è mica difficile! – Hai mica visto le mie chiavi?
eintraege.info: Adds emphasis to a negative sentence. In a question it means by any chance. Typical of spoken Italian.

eintraege.std: forse; ah, se fosse così (maybe; I wish)
eintraege.bsp: Vieni alla festa? – Magari! Ma devo lavorare.
eintraege.info: Alone, Magari! means I wish! Before a verb it can mean maybe: magari vengo domani. The tone shows which one.

eintraege.bsp: Dai, andiamo, siamo in ritardo!
eintraege.info: To encourage, to persuade, or to show mild disbelief or impatience. Very frequent.

eintraege.std: va bene, è accettabile (that's fair, that works)
eintraege.bsp: Un caffè dopo cena? Ci sta.
eintraege.info: Common in speech, especially among younger speakers. Not in writing.

eintraege.bsp: Che figo questo telefono!
eintraege.info: Very common and friendly among friends. The word comes from a vulgar one, so some older people don't like it; at the office use bello, bravo, interessante.

eintraege.std: per esempio; circa (like, for example, about)
eintraege.bsp: Ho comprato tipo dieci chili di pasta.
eintraege.info: Used like English like, also as a filler. A little goes a long way.

eintraege.std: vale a dire (that is, I mean)
eintraege.bsp: Cioè, non mi hai ascoltato per niente?
eintraege.info: Meaning that is, but in speech also a filler to correct or to explain yourself.

eintraege.std: ma no, per niente (no way, of course not)
eintraege.bsp: Hai freddo? – Macché, sto benissimo.
eintraege.info: A strong, friendly no. Often with a gesture.

eintraege.std: così così; in breve (so-so; in short)
eintraege.bsp: Come stai? – Insomma.
eintraege.info: As an answer, Insomma means not great, not bad. At the start of a sentence it can mean in short.

eintraege.bsp: Mannaggia, ho perso il treno!
eintraege.info: Mild and common; it comes from the south but you'll hear it everywhere. Not rude.

eintraege.std: di niente, non c'è problema (don't mention it)
eintraege.bsp: Grazie mille! – Figurati!
eintraege.info: Informal (tu). To an older person or a stranger: Si figuri.

gruppen.intro: In class you learn the normal words. You will still hear these a lot: you need to understand them, but you don't have to say them.

eintraege.bsp: C'è un sacco di gente in coda.
eintraege.info: Neutral-informal. Also un mucchio di, una marea di.

eintraege.bsp: Questa bici costa un botto.
eintraege.info: Informal. botto also means bang, so the context decides.

eintraege.bsp: Per l'affitto spendo una cifra.
eintraege.info: Not the digit! una cifra, used alone, is a big sum, often too big: Costa una cifra.

eintraege.bsp: Ho pagato questo vestito due soldi.
eintraege.info: For something cheap or small. Also: un'inezia.

eintraege.bsp: Per la bolletta ho pagato un centone.
eintraege.info: Informal. You'll hear it in markets and among friends.

eintraege.bsp: Alla fine ho dovuto sganciare cinquanta euro.
eintraege.info: Informal and a bit grumbling. Also: scucire (soldi).

eintraege.bsp: Dopo il divorzio è finito sul lastrico.
eintraege.info: Colloquial and rather strong; for a serious money problem, not for a bad week.

eintraege.std: in piccole somme nel tempo (in instalments)
eintraege.bsp: Ho comprato la lavatrice a rate.
eintraege.info: Everyday. At the shop you'll be asked: Paga in contanti o a rate?

gruppen.intro: Slang changes fast. Young people use it with each other. An adult who uses it at the office often sounds strange.

eintraege.bsp: Raga, che facciamo stasera?
eintraege.info: Short for ragazzi; for a mixed group of friends. Also used in messages.

eintraege.bsp: Bella! Come va?
eintraege.info: A greeting among young friends, mostly north and centre. It has nothing to do with beauty here.

eintraege.std: che fatica, che noia (what a drag)
eintraege.bsp: Domani devo alzarmi alle sei, che sbatti!
eintraege.info: Young speakers. Also: sbattimento.

eintraege.bsp: Se non trovo il passaporto, sclero!
eintraege.info: Informal; from sclerotico. Said jokingly.

eintraege.bsp: Questa canzone spacca!
eintraege.info: Literally to split. In slang: to be great. With friends only.

eintraege.bsp: Dopo tre ore di coda sono sbroccato.
eintraege.info: Strong anger or stress. Young and informal.

eintraege.bsp: Non fare lo sfigato, vieni anche tu!
eintraege.info: It can hurt. Among friends it's a joke; never use it about someone you don't know.

eintraege.bsp: Quel video è troppo cringe.
eintraege.info: English loanword, said as in English. Mostly young speakers.

eintraege.bsp: Mi ha ghostato dopo il primo appuntamento.
eintraege.info: English loanword with an Italian verb ending (ghostare, ho ghostato). Dating and messaging.

eintraege.std: un discorso lungo e noioso (a long boring lecture)
eintraege.bsp: Mio padre mi ha fatto un pippone sui compiti.
eintraege.info: Informal; at home or among friends. Don't use it about your boss.

gruppen.intro: You'll hear swear words in Italy on TV, in films, in traffic and at the café, often from people who don't mean any harm. You should understand them, but saying them yourself is risky: as a foreigner you can quickly sound aggressive or ridiculous. The mildest words are marked 1, the strongest 3.

eintraege.std: Che noia! Che seccatura! (What a bore!)
eintraege.bsp: Un'altra riunione? Che palle!
eintraege.info: Very common among friends and colleagues. Mild-strong; not for a boss or a stranger.

eintraege.std: una parola al posto di cazzo (a softer swear word)
eintraege.bsp: Ma che cavolo fai?
eintraege.info: A polite replacement for the stronger word. Fine with most people. Also: caspita, accidenti.

eintraege.bsp: Porca miseria, ho dimenticato il portafoglio!
eintraege.info: A softened swear. You hear it everywhere, also from older people.

eintraege.std: persona che dà fastidio (a pain in the neck)
eintraege.bsp: Mio cugino è un rompiscatole.
eintraege.info: Playful, not an insult for most people. Also: scocciatore.

eintraege.bsp: Vai a quel paese, ho da fare!
eintraege.info: A polite way to send someone away. It still sounds rude.

eintraege.bsp: Questo bagno è sporco, che schifo!
eintraege.info: Common and not a swear word, but harsh about a person or their work.

eintraege.std: non mi importa niente (I couldn't care less)
eintraege.bsp: Se arrivi tardi, me ne frego.
eintraege.info: Rude to say to a person. It also has a political history (the fascist motto me ne frego), so it can sound heavy.

eintraege.bsp: Ma che cazzo dici? – Non capisco un cazzo.
eintraege.info: A very strong word (it literally names a body part) that Italians use all the time in everyday speech. A foreigner who says it can sound aggressive. Understand it, don't use it.

eintraege.bsp: Che merda di giornata!
eintraege.info: Strong but very common when you are angry about a situation. Not about a person's work in their presence.

eintraege.bsp: Sono incazzato nero: mi hanno cancellato il volo.
eintraege.info: Strong but extremely common. Friends and family only.

eintraege.bsp: Si è comportato da stronzo con me.
eintraege.info: A real insult to one person: never say it to someone's face unless you want a fight.

eintraege.bsp: Vaffanculo, lasciami stare!
eintraege.info: Very strong and also used between friends as a joke; you can't tell which from outside. Don't say it. If it's said to you, it is not polite.

eintraege.std: (swearing with the name of God or the Madonna)
eintraege.bsp: In alcune regioni si sentono spesso, ma sono pesanti: meglio non ripeterle.
eintraege.info: You will hear them (more in some regions) from people who don't mean to offend. Many Italians still find them deeply offensive. Never repeat them.

hoeflich.zu: Potresti abbassare un po' la voce, per favore?
Mi dà un momento, per favore?
